figures.title: Figure 1
figures.llm_description: FIG. 1. A schematic showing the crystal structure of a TMD monolayer (MX2) with (a) top view and (b) side view. The transition metal (M) and chalcogen (X) atoms are represented by purple (large) and yellow (small) spheres, respectively. The unit cell (red) and the orthogonal supercell (blue) are also depicted in (a). The armchair and zigzag orientations corre-spond to x and y directions, respectively.

figures.title: Figure 2
figures.llm_description: FIG. 2. Tensile stress σ as a function of uniaxial strain ε along (a) armchair and (b) zigzag directions, respectively, for monolayer MX2 (M = Mo, W; X = S, Se, Te) TMDs. Solid and dashed lines are used for WX2 and MoX2, respectively.

figures.title: Figure 3
figures.llm_description: FIG. 3. Total and projected density of states for strain-free monolayer MX2 (M = Mo, W; X = S, Se, Te) TMDs. For the transition metal M and the chalcogen X, the density of states are projected onto s, p, d and s, p orbitals, respectively. The Fermi level is set to zero.

figures.title: Figure 4
figures.llm_description: FIG. 4. Bonding charge density for monolayer MX2 (M = Mo, W; X = S, Se, Te) TMDs, obtained as the charge density difference between the valence charge density of the monolayer and the superposition of the valence charge density of the neutral constituent atoms. Red and blue colors indicate the electron accumulation and depletion, respectively. The color scale is in the units of e/Bohr3.

figures.title: Figure 5
figures.llm_description: FIG. 5. Variation of (a) the Young’s modulus and (b) the ultimate strength of monolayer MX2 (M = Mo, W; X = S, Se, Te) TMDs with the charge transfer ∆Q from transition metal M to chalcogens X.

tables.title: Table 2
tables.content: TABLE II. Calculated Young’s modulus E (GPa), ultimate strength σ∗(GPa), ultimate strain ε∗corresponding to the ultimate strength for armchair and zigzag directions, anisotropy factor φ and the charge transfer ∆Q (e) from M to X for strain-free MX2 monolayer sheets.
